newsitem.title: FINLAND: LIPPONEN SAYS INFO SOCIETY CREATES JOBS.
newsitem.headline: LIPPONEN SAYS INFO SOCIETY CREATES JOBS.

text.p: Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Monday that the information society was -- far from destroying jobs -- generating opportunities for more.
"The development of the information society is in fact creating better conditions for an increase in jobs," Lipponen told a seminar in the text of a prepared speech.

"Whereas the creation of new jobs in 1960 to 1973 required economic growth of over 4.2 percent, during the past 20 years new jobs have been created when growth surpassed the two percent threshold," Lipponen said.
"Today jobs are lost expressly because of old technology and they are created by new technology that produces more labour-intensive growth," he said.
"The training challenge is enormous and the investment in continous job training is Europe's most important challenge," Lipponen said.

He referred to a European Commission estimate that about 80 percent of the technology in use in the year 2005 will be less than 10 years old, whereas 80 percent of the workforce will have training dating back over 10 years.
